transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-29 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Rahul Singh (Redwood SE), Marta Lee (Equinox Channel Lead), Carlos Ruiz (Equinox Co-sell Rep), Ravi Patel (Equinox SE)

Summary: quick pipeline sync, review of top deals, technical blockers, agree on pilots and next steps

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lena): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick agenda - run through the top six deals, call out blockers and then confirm pilots.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Marta): Thanks Lena. yeah and we also wanted to talk through partner pricing tiers, some of our AEs asked around discounts for dedicated capacity.
00:29 Speaker 1 (Lena): totally, we'll cover pricing. Rahul you'll start on the technical items?
00:33 Speaker 3 (Rahul): yeah happy to. so i've been looking at the top two deals - finance customer and a healthcare provider. main concern is latency for the finance real-time use case and EU data residency for healthcare.
00:50 Speaker 4 (Ravi): for the healthcare one, data residency is hard requirement, we might need private deployment or VPC option. can you recap Redwood's private offering quickly?
01:02 Speaker 3 (Rahul): sure - Redwood Private gives a customer-managed control plane, VPC peering, and optionally an on-prem package. there's a KMS/HSM integration for key management, and audit logging. couple of notes - the private setup has longer lead time and there are ops costs.
01:20 Speaker 2 (Marta): OK, that's expected. for finance, the AE wants sub-200ms tail latency for a 512 token prompt at 95th percentile is that plausible on hosted?
01:33 Speaker 3 (Rahul): depends. hosted can hit low latencies for smaller models with adequate capacity. for guaranteed SLOs we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated for those high tail-SLOs; the difference is dedicated gives reserved GPU pools so you don't get noisy neighbor spikes. also we can do model quantization and batching configs to reduce latency/cost.
01:54 Speaker 4 (Carlos): do you have benchmarks comparing hosted vs dedicated? our AEs keep asking for numbers to justify premium pricing.
02:03 Speaker 3 (Rahul): i will share a short benchmark doc - i ran a sample on a gpt-like open model and saw 30% lower p95 when pinned to dedicated infra with consistent batch sizing. caveat: results vary by model, sequence length, and kernel choices - our runtime picks kernels based on arch and seq distribution.
02:22 Speaker 1 (Lena): note - Rahul will drop the benchmark spreadsheet and quickstart scripts.
02:28 Speaker 2 (Marta): thanks. another blocker - procurement asked about SOC2 and ISO. can you confirm Redwood has SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001?
02:38 Speaker 3 (Rahul): yes SOC2 type II, ISO 27001 in progress but we have controls and can share the security pack; also support for SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs.
02:51 Speaker 4 (Ravi): small transcription hiccup here: last time our note said 'K V cash' - that's KV cache right?
03:00 Speaker 3 (Rahul): yes KV cache, sorry the auto transcript mangled it. cache helps for prefix reuse and can cut token cost in half for chatty flows.
03:12 Speaker 2 (Carlos): for pricing tiers, how do partner discounts work for co-sell pilots?
03:18 Speaker 1 (Lena): we have a pilot discount for first 3 months and then partner revenue share on closed deals. we'll send the exact numbers, but it's flexible depending on deal size and whether they go dedicated or private.
03:34 Speaker 2 (Marta): great. let's walk through the six opportunities quickly - i've grouped them by timeline (Q3/Q4).
03:42 Speaker 2 (Marta): Opportunity A (finance, priority): expected decision by mid-august, technical contact is Ravi, success criteria are p95 < 200ms and monthly cost under $5k for MVP.
03:59 Speaker 4 (Ravi): on our side we can run a short spike with 1k concurrency tests, but will need sample prompts and some synthetic traffic.
04:10 Speaker 3 (Rahul): perfect - we'll provide a quickstart script and a small harness. for the p95 target i'd recommend a dedicated 1-2 GPU setup for consistent tail behavior.
04:24 Speaker 2 (Carlos): Opportunity B (healthcare): compliance is must, timeline end of Q3, customer wants on-prem or VPC-only.
04:33 Speaker 3 (Rahul): for on-prem we need procurement lead time - typically 6-8 weeks from contract to deployed test environment, can be faster if infra is ready.
04:44 Speaker 1 (Lena): ok we'll flag that timeline in the GTM materials.
04:49 Speaker 2 (Marta): Opportunity C is a mid-market SaaS looking for embeddings for semantic search, lower latency requirements but large usage - cost becomes primary concern.
05:02 Speaker 3 (Rahul): those are perfect for hosted with caching and batching; we can also recommend quantized model variants to reduce cost per token.
05:12 Speaker 2 (Marta): any red flags on integrations? they use AWS and EKS, but no on-prem - seems straightforward.
05:21 Speaker 3 (Rahul): straightforward, we have cloud regions for NA and EU; for EU residency we can route requests to EU region. for stronger guarantees we suggest Redwood Dedicated or Private pinned to EU infra.
05:35 Speaker 4 (Carlos): customers sometimes ask about fallback policies if a model is down - is there auto routing to cheaper models?
05:42 Speaker 3 (Rahul): yep smart routing supports policy-based routing by latency, cost, region, and tier. automatic fallback to compatible model variants is supported.
05:55 Speaker 2 (Marta): great. let's talk pilot mechanics: what does Redwood need vs what Equinox should own?
06:03 Speaker 1 (Lena): proposed split: Redwood provides runtime access, pilot credits, benchmark scripts, and a technical SE to support spikes; Equinox owns customer introductions, AE motions, and initial integration work. we'll co-author an onboarding checklist.
06:18 Speaker 4 (Ravi): about instrumentation - we need token-level cost breakdowns and latencies to show to customers.
06:27 Speaker 3 (Rahul): Redwood Console shows per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost and latency. we can give demo access for the pilot.
06:36 Speaker 2 (Carlos): on the sales motion, can Equinox use Redwood sales deck as is or do you prefer joint deck?
06:41 Speaker 1 (Lena): we have a partner-ready deck; we'll share a joint GTM one-pager and a templated co-sell pitch. we'll ask Equinox to customize customer logos and use cases.
06:53 Speaker 2 (Marta): any major competitive intel to be aware of? we had one customer leaning to Anthropic for model quality, and another looking at OpenAI primarily for simplicity.
07:04 Speaker 3 (Rahul): noted. our differentiation should be production-first metrics and deployment flexibility. mention dedicated SLA and on-prem options.
07:15 Speaker 2 (Marta): agreed.
07:20 Speaker 1 (Lena): ok time check - 10 min left, let's confirm owners for three pilot accounts.
07:24 Speaker 2 (Marta): Account 1 - finance (Ravi to lead), Account 2 - healthcare (Carlos to intro), Account 3 - SaaS embeddings (Marta will own).
07:36 Speaker 3 (Rahul): i'll start the benchmark runs this week and post results. i'll include p50/p90/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
07:45 Speaker 4 (Ravi): do you have an example of a canary rollout for models? customer asked about rollback safety.
07:52 Speaker 3 (Rahul): yes we've got rollout primitives - canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. we can demo in the next technical deep dive.
08:04 Speaker 1 (Lena): agreed - schedule a technical deep dive next week for Ravi and their infra team.
08:12 Speaker 2 (Marta): final ask - can you send over SOC2 package and the partner pricing tiers?
08:18 Speaker 1 (Lena): yes, i'll include those in the follow-up along with the benchmark sheet and the joint GTM one-pager.
08:26 Speaker 2 (Marta): perfect. thanks all.
08:30 Speaker 1 (Lena): quick recap of next steps - Lena to send materials, Equinox to confirm priority accounts, Rahul to run benchmarks. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had occasional name swaps and phonetic errors (e.g., 'K V cash' instead of KV cache). Some timestamps approximate.
